oppforinger.html: • [external — Hansen et al.] Possible void-stacked ISW anomaly at low redshift (arXiv:2506.08832). Frode K. Hansen et al., University of Oslo + Argentina. Relevance: qualitatively similar in sign-structure to the EFC void ISW sign-flip prediction in 31942677; quantitative confrontation (amplitude, δ-binning, z-dependence) pending as a separate EFC working note. Status: not yet tested by EFC.

• [external — DESI Collaboration] DESI DR1 modified-gravity constraints (arXiv:2411.12026). Relevance: background-sector MG signal consistent with zero, used as a constraint on the EFC perturbation survival valley (μ0 ∈ [0.93, 0.96]) rather than as evidence for it. Status: consistent with EFC L0/L1 reduction; no EFC working note yet.

• [external — eROSITA Collaboration] eROSITA cluster-abundance growth-of-structure analysis (arXiv:2410.09499). Relevance: independent S8 determination relevant to the perturbation survival valley and to the DES–KiDS bifurcation already noted in §4 (P3 PASS entry). Status: contextual; no EFC working note yet.

• [external — review article] S8 tension landscape review 2026 (arXiv:2602.12238). Relevance: synthesises the current DES low / KiDS+eROSITA high / HSC intermediate split. Cited only as background context for any future EFC “S8 Landscape Update” note.
• [external — Srinivasan et al.] Forecast study (arXiv:2603.11895). Relevance: contextual forecast, not a measurement. Will be cited if and when an EFC working note targets the same observable.

• [external — KiDS-Legacy Collaboration] Joint analysis of second- and third-order cosmic shear in the final Kilo-Degree Survey data release (arXiv:2606.12389). COSEBIs at 2′–300′ combined with third-order aperture mass moments give Ωm = 0.297+0.056−0.040 and S8 = 0.806+0.025−0.023, more than doubling the figure of merit in the Ωm–S8 plane relative to the two-point analysis alone. The third-order measurements pass the internal consistency tests and agree with Planck within 1σ, which the authors state as providing no evidence for an S8 tension. Relevance to EFC: bears on P4, where S8 ≈ 0.82 (robust, downward) is fixed by the growth-sector coupling-structure closure (32084670) with no free-parameter escape route. The measured value is consistent with the EFC figure within 1σ — but it is equally consistent with Planck, so it does not discriminate between them. Its bearing is on the argument rather than the number: any reading in which a low S8 is itself taken as support for P4 is weakened, because this analysis finds no tension to explain. It also sharpens the DES–KiDS bifurcation noted in §4 (P3 PASS entry) and sits alongside the eROSITA and S8-landscape entries above. Status: no EFC working note yet.

• [external — Liu, Zhang & Liu] “Onsite Calibration of the Shear-Shear Correlation” (arXiv:2606.18705). An onsite-calibrated Fourier-Quad analysis of HSC PDR3 finds S8 = 0.740+0.030−0.030 and Ωm = 0.383+0.129−0.132. The authors report that shear bias varies with photometric-redshift bin, S/N cut, optical band, and estimator, while calibrated constraints remain consistent across the cases examined. Relevance to EFC: this is directly relevant to P4’s cosmic-shear S8 observable and is lower than the robust EFC value S8 ≈ 0.82, so it weakens any claim that the existing low-S8 pattern is already a stable quantitative match. It does not by itself falsify P4 or establish a discrepancy: the HSC result is not directly comparable to DES Y6, KiDS-Legacy, or the sealed Rubin/Euclid test without a matched systematics and estimator study. Insight boundary: the result comments on the empirical robustness of the S8 compilation; it does not change what EFC is responsible for or alter the pre-registered P4 threshold. Status: limitation noted; no EFC working note yet.

oppforinger.html: • [external — DESI Collaboration] DESI DR2 Lyα forest full-shape AP and cosmological-constraint results (arXiv:2607.27410), with the accompanying pre-unblinding validation (arXiv:2607.27411). The analysis combines Lyα–Lyα auto-correlations with Lyα–quasar cross-correlations and reports full-shape AP distances DM/rd = 39.32 ± 0.33 and DH/rd = 8.600 ± 0.066 at the effective redshift; the central value shifts toward ΛCDM relative to the preceding BAO-only result, with substantially tighter uncertainty. Relevance to EFC: this constrains the background expansion and weakens any simple reading of the earlier DESI dynamical-dark-energy preference, but it does not test P1, P3, P4, P6, P7, or P8. Despite the “full-shape” label, the validation found a significant mock bias in fσ8 and excluded that measurement from the final analysis, so this is not a direct P2 (fσ8(z = 0.7)) result and carries no P1–P8 verdict. Status: external constraint; no EFC working note yet.

• [external — Mu, Zhou & Li] Hierarchical Gaussian-process reconstruction of the DESI DR2 late-time expansion history (arXiv:2607.23593). Combining DESI DR2 BAO, compressed Planck distance priors, Pantheon+ and 37 cosmic-chronometer points gives w(z≈0) = −0.80+0.26−0.23; on the same compressed-Planck pipeline, CPL improves over ΛCDM by only Δχ2 ∼ 1. The authors report that the result is sensitive to the compression and does not address the full Planck likelihood. Relevance to EFC: this is not a direct test of any pre-registered prediction P1–P8. It instead weakens the evidential reading of the DESI dynamical-dark-energy signal that has been used as contextual motivation for an L2–L3 background transition. The finding does not change what EFC is responsible for; it lowers the external premise’s weight and leaves the full-likelihood DESI question open. Status: contextual negative/qualifying result; no EFC working note yet.

• [external — Ferri, Ruchika & Melchiorri] “Present Day Cosmic Acceleration from SDSS and DESI BAO: A Call for Finer Tomography of the DESI Bright Galaxy Survey” (arXiv:2607.07348). DESI+Planck gives q0 = 0.10+0.21−0.23, whereas SDSS+Planck gives q0 = −0.22+0.20−0.21; adding Pantheon+ returns q0 to negative values. The authors attribute the difference mainly to the lowest effective redshift sampled (zeff ≈ 0.295 for DESI versus ≈ 0.15 for SDSS), and propose finer DESI tomography. Relevance to EFC: this is a caution relevant to P7’s H0 three-window interpretation and to background-level comparisons associated with P6: redshift coverage and CPL extrapolation must be separated from an EFC-specific regime effect. It does not measure the P7 three-window decomposition, does not test the P6 sign lemma, and provides neither support nor falsification of either prediction. Insight boundary: it changes the evidential weight assigned to a BAO-only redshift-dependent difference, not what EFC is responsible for. Status: limitation noted; no EFC working note yet.

• [external — Euclid Consortium / ESA] Euclid Quick Data Release 2 (Q2), published 24 June 2026 (Euclid Consortium; ESA documentation). Q2 contains VIS calibrated images plus astrometry and photometry catalogues for 60 million stars across 4.8 deg2 in the Galactic Bulge Survey. It is not a cosmic-shear, EG, or gravitational-slip release. Relevance to EFC: this does not match any pre-registered prediction P1–P8 and provides neither support nor falsification. It is an informational staging release only; it does not change what EFC is responsible for, the sealed Euclid DR1 benchmark, or any P1–P8 status. Insight boundary: no new EFC obligation is created beyond keeping the distinct DR1 cosmic-shear release and its frozen prediction clearly separated from Q2. Status: logged as external context; no EFC working note and no evidence-register entry.

• [external — Dixon et al.] “The Peculiar Growth of Structure: Validating fσ8 Measurements from TITAN Type Ia Supernovae and the Uchuu Simulations” (arXiv:2606.14962). TITAN/Uchuu end-to-end mocks recover fσ8 = 0.429±0.038 from a simulated input of 0.428, with statistical and systematic contributions reported separately. Relevance to EFC: the recovered central value is close to P2’s sealed 0.430 point, but this is a method-validation result on simulated input, not an observation of P2 at z = 0.7. Insight boundary: it informs whether a local SN peculiar-velocity pipeline can recover its input; it does not change what EFC is responsible for, provide an independent P2 verdict, or alter the pre-registered threshold. Status: method validation noted; no EFC working note yet.

• [external — Cha et al. 2025] “A High-Caliber View of the Bullet Cluster through JWST Strong and Weak Lensing Analyses”, ApJ 987, L15 (arXiv:2503.21870). 146 strong-lensing constraints from 37 systems + 398 sources/arcmin² weak lensing; main-cluster mass distribution highly elongated (NW–SE) with at least three subclumps; possible mass+ICL trail; new SIDM upper bound σ/m < 0.5 cm²/g (tightest single-cluster bound to date). Relevance to EFC: bears on the cluster merger geometry structural test (31173850) and on the SPARC k = 0.415 screening cross-check used in 31940469. The tightening σ/m bound is consistent with the EFC postulate of no DM particles, but this is a structural consistency, not a confirmation. Status: confronted in 31963668 (EFC-VAL-2026-004).

• [external — Rihtaršič et al. 2026] “Mapping dark matter in the Bullet Cluster using JWST imaging and spectroscopy” (arXiv:2601.22245). Updated lens model from JWST NIRCam + NIRSpec, constrained by 135 secure multiple images from 27 background galaxies with spectroscopic redshifts (z = 0.9–6.7); main cluster modelled as elongated double-peaked distribution; subcluster as a single large-scale halo with ~4 kpc BCG offset. Relevance to EFC: directly enables a high-fidelity recalibration of the pre-registered Asig shock-front lensing-asymmetry estimator (planned EFC test, see §5). Before this work only 6 systems had spec-z — 27 is a qualitative jump that makes the Asig test feasible. Status: confronted in 31963668 (EFC-VAL-2026-004); PIEMD Asig baseline null (p = 0.98) validates the test operator; full Asig on free-form δκ residual pending Cha et al. κ-map acquisition.

• [external — Cho et al. 2025] “Joint JWST–DECam Lensing Reveals That the Bullet Cluster Is a Minor Merger” (arXiv:2512.03150). First robust virial masses for the three individual Bullet Cluster components from combined weak+strong lensing with JWST/NIRCam and DECam: M200c = 15.11×1014 M⊙ (main) and 1.49×1014 M⊙ (sub) — mass ratio ~10:1, i.e. a minor merger rather than the previously assumed 2:1 or 3:1. Relevance to EFC: changes the geometric baseline of the cluster merger geometry structural exclusion test (31173850); a minor merger implies weaker ram-pressure, easier mass–gas separation, and a different operating point for the Θ(ρ) screening profile along the merger axis. Status: confronted in 31963668 (EFC-VAL-2026-004); 10:1 ratio strengthens the structural exclusion test (31173850), not weakens it.
